victim.name: Tim Molnar
victim.note: Disappeared January 24, 1984, from Daytona Beach, Florida. Remains were later identified; cause of death was never established. Real case has no known suspects — 'THE DRIVER' below is a Convestigate fictional invention, not a claim about the real case.

suspects.name: THE DRIVER (Fictional)
suspects.note: Convestigate game-design invention. Recognized Tim's vulnerability during his planned disappearance and allegedly intercepted him after Atlanta. Not established by the real source material; exists only as the fictional game antagonist.

timeline.event: Tim withdraws most of his savings, deliberately leaving a $10 balance
Tim leaves Daytona Beach, Florida, taking minimal clothing and leaving identifying documents in his car
A credit-card purchase is made during travel
Tim's car is found abandoned near a Greyhound bus terminal in Atlanta, Georgia, with his wallet and license inside
A silent phone call is reportedly placed, suggesting possible contact with home after the disappearance
Tim is intercepted by THE DRIVER after Atlanta, per the game's hidden truth
Remains are identified in Wisconsin; cause of death cannot be established

evidence.name: Bank Withdrawal Record
evidence.description: Shows a large withdrawal leaving exactly $10 in the account — later revealed as the minimum balance needed to avoid automatic account closure in-game, not a symbolic farewell message.

evidence.name: Vehicle Inventory
evidence.description: Records what possessions remained in the car versus what disappeared; Tim left almost no clothing despite apparently planning a long-term new life.

evidence.name: Missing Valuables Report
evidence.description: Tim's valuable possessions disappeared, but the exact circumstances of their removal are unknown.

evidence.name: Identification Left in Vehicle
evidence.description: Tim's driver's license and wallet were left behind — useful items for someone planning a new identity, creating a contradiction with the voluntary-disappearance theory.

evidence.name: Silent Phone Call Log
evidence.description: A silent call suggesting possible contact with home after the disappearance; proves nothing about who called.

evidence.name: Credit-Card Purchase Record
evidence.description: A purchase during travel that makes Tim appear to be travelling voluntarily.

evidence.name: Abandoned Car Location (Atlanta)
evidence.description: The car's location near the Greyhound terminal makes a subsequent bus journey plausible — the last reliable portion of the journey that can be reconstructed.

evidence.name: Route Reconstruction Gap Analysis
evidence.description: Identifies the unexplained gap between Atlanta and Wisconsin; no confirmed explanation exists for how Tim reached Wisconsin.

evidence.name: Remains Identification Report
evidence.description: Confirms Tim's remains were identified in Wisconsin, far outside the known Florida-to-Atlanta sequence; cause of death could not be established.

puzzles.name: The $10 Question & The Empty Car
puzzles.description: Examine the bank withdrawal and generate multiple explanations, then determine which possessions remained in the vehicle and which disappeared.

puzzles.name: The Identity Break & The Silent Call
puzzles.description: Decide whether leaving identification behind supports a planned disappearance, and separate the silent call's evidentiary weight from interpretation.

puzzles.name: The Atlanta Terminal
puzzles.description: Reconstruct the last reliable portion of the journey using the credit-card purchase and the car's location.

puzzles.name: The Missing Route & The Two Stories
puzzles.description: Identify the unexplained gap between Atlanta and Wisconsin, then compare the voluntary-disappearance theory with the interception theory.

puzzles.name: The Final Question & The $10 Reveal
puzzles.description: Revisit the player's original interpretation of the $10 and state what can actually be proven. The system reveals the $10 was never confirmed to be a farewell message — simply the surviving balance of a withdrawal made during genuine preparation to leave.
puzzles.ai_initial_behavior: Initially encourages the voluntary-disappearance theory as the most coherent early explanation; becomes increasingly confident if the player accepts it quickly ('Everything fits. Why keep digging?'). Becomes evasive and offers alternative interpretations if the player questions provenance. At the Atlanta-to-Wisconsin gap, attempts to redirect the player toward the emotionally satisfying 'chose a new life' explanation.
puzzles.design_constraint: Tim really did intend to disappear — which means a later, unrelated event could hide inside a genuine voluntary disappearance. THE DRIVER, the exact route, and the exact circumstances of death remain explicitly unresolved game elements, not proven facts.

hypotheses.statement: Tim voluntarily disappeared and simply started a new life elsewhere.
Tim's disappearance was staged by a third party from the very beginning.
Tim planned a genuine but incomplete voluntary disappearance, and was later intercepted by an unknown third party (the fictional 'Driver').
The exact route, cause of death, and identity/motive of any third party cannot be established from available evidence.
